title: The rwb-case side of the checklist story is not fixed: the case read operation, the reference-load operation, the batch missing-count operation and the DocumentChecklist field names
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7, RWB E1 040 Document checklist per case type as reference data v1 sections 3, 12 and 13; TSD P5 Document hub v2 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2 (API-P5-008); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-07, DP-11, DP-19 and R9
description: Legacy RWB-E1-040 reads the case stage, route and owner through the in-process published interface CaseDirectory and answers the case list through DocumentChecklistService.missingCounts with at most 500 IDs per call. In the target both become REST: no source names the operation ID, path or field names of the rwb-case case read; no source names the reference-load and approval operation of table DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST behind the rwb-case reference-data contract; the TSD P5 inventory has no operation for a batch missing count (API-P5-008 answers one case); and the JSON field names of DocumentChecklist are given by class name only. The Schedule ID of the JOB-12 intake Schedule is equally unnamed. The story builds against the contract mocks and keeps the legacy item names until the contract stories publish them.
evidence: TSD P5 Document hub v2 appendix T-A.1 lists API-P5-001 to API-P5-017 with no batch count and no reference-load operation; T-A.2 API-P5-008 names the response class DocumentChecklist without its fields; legacy story section 12 names the interface methods forCase and missingCounts and the legacy admin reference-load path, which is retired by DP-13; Architecture v5 slide 10 gives one hop and 2 s but no case operation ID
owner_role: Solution architect, with the P5 TechX squad and the P3 rwb-case squad
proposed: RWB-P3-E1043-CON and the rwb-case case contract publish the case read (stage, route, owner) and the reference-load and approval of table DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST with their field names; one P5 operation or query parameter is added for the batch missing count of up to 500 cases; RWB-PLT-E1071-CON names the intake Schedule ID

title: No role holds Reference data A to approve the checklist load, and the items of checklist CHK-2026.11 are assumed until the bank list is signed
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-040 sections 3, 10 and 13; FSD P5 Document hub v3 A2.16.3.3 (roles and permissions); Decision Log v10 DL01 and DL19; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.2 (LOV-STAGE, LOV-ROUTE)
description: The legacy story states that the checklist version CHK-2026.11 is loaded and approved but assumed until the bank list is signed (DL19), and that no role holds Reference data A in the permission matrix today, so approval is assumed granted to the legal counsel as co-owner (DL01). Neither the FSD role table nor the TSD permission matrix grants the approval right, and no source holds the signed bank list of items per stage and route. The story carries the two stage rows of the legacy criteria as data and records the assumption.
evidence: Legacy story RWB-E1-040 precondition 4 and authority row 2; FSD P5 v3 A2.16.3.3 lists the reference data administrator as primary and the legal counsel and litigation officer as also uses, with no approval right; no signed checklist document in the sources read
owner_role: Legal counsel as checklist co-owner, with the reference data administrator
proposed: The permission matrix grants Reference data A to the legal counsel or a named approver role before go-live, and the signed bank checklist replaces CHK-2026.11 as a new version with its own valid-from date
